rationale: The profile indicates a small, self-contained BenchmarkGame program (puzzle) with few or no extractable function-level features, so the table should favor passes with strong security/diversity payoff per unit of overhead rather than blanket heavy transformation. SUB and BCF get the highest SecurityGain because arithmetic and control-flow obfuscation give the best reverse-engineering resistance on small compute-bound programs, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept low-moderate since puzzle-style benchmarks execute tight loops where BCF in particular can multiply runtime; the moderate values signal the pass is welcome only where the cost dimension of the function profile tolerates it. FLA and IBR receive mid weights — flattening and branch injection add meaningful diversity on control-flow-heavy solver code but carry real size/runtime overhead in hot loops. SPLIT and IGV are cheap, low-risk layout/diversity transformations and are kept enabled with low cost weights, letting them apply broadly to pad structural diversity without measurable slowdown. ICALL is retained with the highest CorrectnessRisk weight (indirect-call rewriting interacts badly with varargs/extern calls common in benchmark-game code) and moderate gains, so it applies only where call-site features are clearly safe. No pass is fully disabled because the program's unknown internal structure means the per-function feature matching should be trusted to gate application; the weight table simply biases the selection toward security gains while keeping cumulative runtime and size overhead acceptable for this small, latency-sensitive benchmark.
